## {#today .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.todaymeta}
The full slide deck in four parts, with the two optional runs in the main flow
:::

:::: {.todaybox}
::: {.nonincremental}
1. Credibility and tools – science, its crisis, and the toolchain
2. The claim and its estimand – the paper in full, estimands, and causal graphs
3. Reproduction and exploration – a recorded result reproduced, and the specification menu worked
4. Multiverse and preregistration – the specification curve read, and one analysis preregistered
:::
::::

::: {.todaytake}
You leave with a reproduced result, an estimand and a graph of your own, a preregistered analysis and your dot on the class chart
:::

::: {.todaymeta}
Work along in your IDE, with the webR workspace as the fallback
:::

::: notes
Welcome. These are the complete slides, with the two optional runs, the methods tutorial and the multiverse tutorial, which a shorter delivery can skip, so they are longer than a single day can hold and are best taken over several sessions. The four parts follow one argument. The first asks why anyone thinks that social science is in trouble and what the tools have to do with it, and the second goes inside one published paper and asks which question its claim answers. In the third you reproduce one of the results recorded in the SCORE robustness study, choosing among three analysts, and then vary it, and the fourth reads the spread of results that those variations produce, before you preregister the one analysis that you would defend.
:::
